title: repair chunk-reassembly for streamed tool-call payloads causing structured-output corruption
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-severity customer reports: in certain hosted and Dedicated/VPC flows, streaming tool-call responses intermittently produce malformed or interleaved JSON fragments which cause the structured-output parser to fail and downstream function invocation to abort. The problem is reproducible when the proxy/gateway produces small TCP/TLS chunks and the runtime's streaming reassembly logic interacts with the KV-cache flush/batching path, resulting in chunk boundaries being attributed to the wrong request on high-concurrency connections.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use the support sample: run the customer workload with >400 concurrent streaming chat requests using the tool_call enabled model variant.
2) Stand up the Envoy test-proxy configured to enable HTTP/1.1 chunking and connection pooling (see test-proxy/conf/chunked.yaml attached), or reproduce with the customer's TLS-offloading LB config.
3) Send requests that trigger function/tool calls with large nested JSON outputs (~2-6 KB) so responses are split into multiple chunks.
4) Observe parser errors in the runtime logs: 'structured_parse: unexpected token at chunk boundary' and failing function invocations with support ticket #{SUP-1972}.
5) Reproduce in Dedicated with VPC peering and in Hosted using the managed gateway to confirm cross-environment behavior.
root_cause: A race between the streaming reassembler and the KV-cache flush path: when a large generated tool payload is emitted, the runtime's micro-batching can cause an intermediate flush which emits a chunk for a different request on the same pooled connection. The reassembly logic assumed per-connection sequentiality for chunks and did not attach per-request sequence markers; under connection multiplexing and certain proxy chunking behaviors, fragments can be interleaved or re-labeled, resulting in malformed concatenations presented to the structured-output parser.
proposed_fix: 1) Patch streaming transport to include a per-request sequence header (X-Runtime-Stream-Id / chunk-seq) for all stream frames so reassembly is always keyed by request even on pooled connections. 2) Harden the parser to tolerate boundary concatenations: attempt incremental parse with rollback and preservation of partial JSON tokens, and reject only when unambiguously corrupt. 3) Add a defensive server-side check that drops/isolates misattributed frames and logs full binary captures for debugging. 4) Short-term hotfix: on Hosted roll out a gate that forces connection affinity for streaming tool-call routes to avoid interleaving until the per-request header is in place.
testing_plan: Unit tests: new parser fuzz harness that generates chunk splits at arbitrary UTF-8/token boundaries (added to runtime/tests/parser_fuzz).
Integration: run the Envoy test-proxy scenario with randomized chunk sizes and aggressive connection pooling for 24h soak in staging. Capture parity between staged and local parser outputs.
E2E: replay customer production traffic capture (anonymized) through patched runtime in a dedicated staging tenant and verify no structured-parse failures across 1M streamed tokens.
Canary: deploy hotfix to 5% of Hosted traffic and to a single non-critical Dedicated customer pool, monitor for parser error rate and function-invoke success metrics for 48h.
release_plan: Short-term: deploy connection-affinity gate to Hosted within 24-48h (runtime-1.23.1-hotfix) and notify affected customers. Medium-term: land per-request stream ID + parser hardening in runtime-1.23.2 and roll out canary -> 50% -> 100% over 1 week. Dedicated/Private customers: provide configuration toggle and coordinate maintenance windows for VPC customers; for on-prem provide patch and upgrade guide. Post-rollback plan: if error rate increases after canary, revert to connection-affinity gate and iterate on parser fixes.
